images.title: Join the prime factors
images.purpose: Show that the prime factors of 12 and 6 put together give the prime factors of 72.
images.composition: Two short rows of dots with their labels side by side on top, one longer row of dots centred below, wide white space between.
images.exact_structure: Top left: 3 teal #0072B2 dots in a row with the label beside them. Top right: 2 amber #E69F00 dots in a row with the label beside them. Below, centred: one row of 5 dots, the first 3 teal and the last 2 amber, all same size and evenly spaced. Exactly 10 dots, no digits inside dots.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec

images.takeaway: Put the prime factors of both numbers together to get the prime factors of 72.
images.description: Three teal dots for 12 and two amber dots for 6 join into one row of five dots that stands for 72.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the dots in each row and say why 3 and 2 make 5 prime factors.

image_decisions.why: Joining the two factor rows is a picture idea; one row-merge image carries it.
